2. `get_cities` listed three "CAN ATTACK" targets that were all actually 3 tiles away; every attack failed with `OUT_OF_RANGE` against the 2-tile city range. The advisory appears to use a wrong or stale distance check. (The units were barbarians and pose no threat to 400 HP walls.)

One-line summary: Locked in four accepted friendships (Russia, Ethiopia, Egypt, Vietnam) to start the Research-Alliance clock and fixed Busan's stalled growth, while leaving the space-race research and spaceport builds on track — units were already spent, and the Congress vote is blocked by a tool that won't return resolution hashes.

steps.text:
Turn 304 actions complete. Here's where things stand.

**What I did:** The headline problem was Daegu — a pop-20 city with 94 production building *literally nothing*. It's now on a Spaceport, which matters because science is my live victory path: I'm tied for the tech lead at 63 techs with Launch Earth Satellite and Moon Landing already unlocked, gated only on spaceport capacity. That makes four spaceports in flight (Gyeongju finishes first at 10 turns), and since space projects run in parallel across spaceports, throughput is the real bottleneck.

I also cleared two piles of idle assets. Margaret Mead was sitting unactivated; she needs a *foreign* campus and pays 1000 Science **and** 1000 Culture, so she's now walking to a valid campus at (80,22) — worth the two-turn trip. And 2031 idle faith bought Alvar Aalto (930f), which advances the Great Engineer pool toward engineers that accelerate space projects. Surplus gold became two builders against a 14-task backlog that only had 6 charges to service it.

**Two things worth knowing:**
- I'm at **peace with everyone**, and nobody is close militarily (2754 vs Macedon's 547). The "can attack" flags on my cities were barbarian/free-city stragglers, all 3 tiles out of a 2-tile range.
- Two ideas I checked and rejected: Daegu and Gwangju both look like they're missing a Seowon (Daegu is pop 20 making just 14 science), and Seowon is dirt cheap at 27 production — but the district advisor reports **no valid placement tiles** in either city, so that science hole can't be fixed.

Gold is still accumulating at +811/turn with no strong sink, and 1784 favor is stranded until the World Congress fires in 27 turns — Diplomatic is a slower path than Science at 10/20 VP, so science remains right.

One caveat: I couldn't write a diary entry. This game has none, and there's no exposed diary-write tool — reflections are recorded inside `end_turn`, which you're running, so that memory won't be captured unless you pass it there.

**Summary:** Put idle Daegu on a 4th Spaceport, sent Margaret Mead for a 1000-science/1000-culture activation, and converted dead faith and gold into a Great Engineer plus two builders — all pushing the science victory while at peace and leading 1373–852.

Done. Here's what happened.

**The blocker is cleared.** There were actually *two* empty policy slots, not the one the repair notice flagged — slot 6 (wildcard) and slot 7 (economic). I filled both to compound the science path:

- **Natural Philosophy** (economic) — doubles Seowon adjacency, stacking on the Five-Year Plan already slotted, across 8 cities
- **Market Economy** (wildcard) — all 7 trade routes are international, so this adds +2 science and +2 culture each, plus gold per resource at destination

Together that's roughly +45 science/turn for zero production cost.

**The bigger picture:** science victory is the recommended path at 60%, and Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are *already tech-unlocked*. The only thing gating a launch is that I have zero completed Spaceports — but four are under construction (Gyeongju in 10 turns, three more at 15), so that's on track rather than a crisis. Building more isn't wasted; parallel spaceports let the later Mars projects run simultaneously.

I also bought a Trader (545g) to fill the idle 8th trade route slot. It couldn't depart — every unit including the new purchase is already out of moves, since the host has run the unit phase — so it'll route to Pella (56 gold, +3 sci, +3 cul) next turn.

**Two things worth flagging for coming turns:**

- **Robert Goddard** (Great Engineer) grants +20% production toward space race projects empire-wide plus a tech boost. My Great Engineer points are 0/660, so I will *never* earn him naturally — patronizing at 10,100g is the only route. I have 1,794g at +811/turn, so he's affordable in ~10 turns, landing right as the first Spaceport completes. I'd recommend banking gold rather than spending it on trinkets until then.
- **1,784 diplomatic favor** is idle at 10/20 DVP, but the next World Congress is 27 turns out, so it can't deploy yet.

No threats: I'm at peace with all 11 civs, and the units near Jeonju/Gwangju are barbarian Field Cannons against 2754 military and 400-HP walls.

**Tooling issue:** `get_cities` reported `>> CAN ATTACK` for targets that were actually 3 tiles away — outside the range-2 city attack, which rejected both with `OUT_OF_RANGE`. The hint appears not to range-check.

**Summary:** Filled both empty policy slots (Natural Philosophy + Market Economy, ~+45 sci/turn) clearing the end-turn blocker, bought a Trader for the idle 8th route slot, and confirmed the science path is on track with 4 Spaceports building — recommend banking gold toward Great Engineer Goddard.

final_summary:
Turn 304 actions complete. Here's where things stand.

**What I did:** The headline problem was Daegu — a pop-20 city with 94 production building *literally nothing*. It's now on a Spaceport, which matters because science is my live victory path: I'm tied for the tech lead at 63 techs with Launch Earth Satellite and Moon Landing already unlocked, gated only on spaceport capacity. That makes four spaceports in flight (Gyeongju finishes first at 10 turns), and since space projects run in parallel across spaceports, throughput is the real bottleneck.

I also cleared two piles of idle assets. Margaret Mead was sitting unactivated; she needs a *foreign* campus and pays 1000 Science **and** 1000 Culture, so she's now walking to a valid campus at (80,22) — worth the two-turn trip. And 2031 idle faith bought Alvar Aalto (930f), which advances the Great Engineer pool toward engineers that accelerate space projects. Surplus gold became two builders against a 14-task backlog that only had 6 charges to service it.

**Two things worth knowing:**
- I'm at **peace with everyone**, and nobody is close militarily (2754 vs Macedon's 547). The "can attack" flags on my cities were barbarian/free-city stragglers, all 3 tiles out of a 2-tile range.
- Two ideas I checked and rejected: Daegu and Gwangju both look like they're missing a Seowon (Daegu is pop 20 making just 14 science), and Seowon is dirt cheap at 27 production — but the district advisor reports **no valid placement tiles** in either city, so that science hole can't be fixed.

Gold is still accumulating at +811/turn with no strong sink, and 1784 favor is stranded until the World Congress fires in 27 turns — Diplomatic is a slower path than Science at 10/20 VP, so science remains right.

One caveat: I couldn't write a diary entry. This game has none, and there's no exposed diary-write tool — reflections are recorded inside `end_turn`, which you're running, so that memory won't be captured unless you pass it there.

**Summary:** Put idle Daegu on a 4th Spaceport, sent Margaret Mead for a 1000-science/1000-culture activation, and converted dead faith and gold into a Great Engineer plus two builders — all pushing the science victory while at peace and leading 1373–852.

steps.text:
Turn 305 actions complete. Civic is now progressing (was empty), income is up to +917/turn, and everything is pointed at the science victory.

**What I did:**
- **Fixed the civic blocker** — nothing was being researched at all. Set **Space Race**, whose boost ("build a Spaceport") will trigger from the four already under construction and halve its cost.
- **Filled an empty policy slot** (slot 7) with Civil Prestige — +1 amenity and +2 housing across my seven governed cities, which also helps district-capped cities grow toward their next district.
- **Bought a Factory in Jeonju (1320g)** — its Industrial Zone only had a Workshop, so this permanently speeds both its Spaceport and every space project after it.
- **Activated Alvar Aalto** at Daegu and sent Margaret Mead to a foreign Seowon at (80,22) to cash in **1000 Science + 1000 Culture** next turn.
- **Dispatched all five idle builders** (lumber mill, mines for the Spaceport cities, deer camp, incense plantation) and started an idle trader on a 56-gold route to Pella.
- **Set both home spies to counterspy** in the Spaceport cities — they couldn't steal tech since I'm the tech leader, so defending Spaceport production from sabotage is the better use.

**Three things worth flagging:**
- **Pingala in Gyeongju has a "Space Initiative" promotion available (+30% production to space projects)**, but I have 0 governor points. This is the single highest-value purchase the moment a point arrives.
- **The `CAN ATTACK` hints in `get_cities` are unreliable** — both the "field cannon" at Jeonju and the "builder" at Pyongyang belong to city-states (Brussels and Cardiff) that I'm at peace with, so neither was actually attackable.
- **Jinju and Gyeongju are both at their specialty district cap** (6 at pop 20), which is why no Industrial Zone or Spaceport can be placed there — not a tooling bug. Jinju needs pop 21; I set it to a Campus project meanwhile.

I reverted one change I'd made: I initially swapped Resource Management for Levée en Masse to cut unit maintenance, then checked resources and put it back — Aluminum income would have dropped from 11 to ~8 against demand 9, and saving ~60g/turn is pointless when I'm at +917.

I did not end the turn, as instructed.

**Plan:** save toward patronizing **Robert Goddard** (Great Engineer, 9950g, ~10 turns) for +20% space-project production empire-wide, timed to land as the first Spaceports complete (Gyeongju in 9 turns).

Turn 306 actions complete. The most important fix was the idle research — Korea was generating 557 science per turn into nothing.

**What I did:**

- **Set research to Guidance Systems** (2 turns, boosted). It was idle. This is also directly on the science-victory path: Guidance Systems + Lasers → Robotics → Smart Materials → Offworld Mission, which is the tech gating the Exoplanet Expedition project.
- **Traded surplus luxuries to Macedon** for Amber, Olives, and Wine (3 new luxury types = +1 amenity each across 4 cities) plus 2 gold and 6 gold/turn. The surplus Diamonds/Incense/Ivory were providing zero benefit. A follow-up attempt for Citrus/Mercury/Tea/Whales was refused, so I stopped there.
- **Dispatched 5 builders** — three were standing on their tasks (Camp on Deer, Plantation on Incense, Mine at Jeonju); two are en route to further work.
- **Activated two Great People** — Alvar Aalto (Great Engineer) at Daegu and Margaret Mead (Great Scientist). Mozart turned out to be spent (0 charges, no free Great Work slots).
- **Sent Great Admiral Matthew Perry** west toward the city-state at (34,12); his ability grants instant suzerainty, worth +1 favor/turn and denying America.
- **Put the idle spy** Do-won on counterspy in the capital (stealing tech is pointless at a 64-vs-52 tech lead).

**Two judgment calls worth flagging:** I did *not* attack the Field Cannon next to Jeonju — it belongs to Brussels, a city-state I'm suzerain of, so the "CAN ATTACK" prompt was a trap that would have started a needless war. And I'm **holding the 1,770 gold** rather than spending it on marginal buildings: Great Engineer Robert Goddard grants +20% production toward space race projects and costs 9,785g, which is ~8 turns away at +941/turn — a far better buy given four spaceports are already under construction (Gyeongju's completes in 7 turns, and Earth Satellite + Moon Landing are already unlocked).

One-line summary: Fixed idle research (Guidance Systems, on the space path), traded dead surplus luxuries to Macedon for 3 new amenity types +6gpt, dispatched all 5 builders, activated 2 Great People, and began banking gold for Robert Goddard's +20% space-project boost while 4 spaceports finish.
